response.sql: WITH order_averages AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_unfilled FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), overall AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS avg_unfilled FROM orderexecutions), above_overall AS (SELECT oa.avg_unfilled FROM order_averages AS oa CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE oa.avg_unfilled > o.avg_unfilled), group_average AS (SELECT AVG(avg_unfilled) AS avg_unfilled FROM above_overall) SELECT AVG(a.avg_unfilled) AS average_order_average, AVG(a.avg_unfilled - o.avg_unfilled) AS average_excess_overall, AVG(a.avg_unfilled - g.avg_unfilled) AS average_excess_group FROM above_overall AS a CROSS JOIN overall AS o CROSS JOIN group_average AS g WHERE a.avg_unfilled > g.avg_unfilled

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is calculated across executions with non-NULL remaincount, so orders with more executions have more weight in that benchmark.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average gives each order equal weight by averaging the per-order averages.
